title: Horseshoe Priors and MDP
summary: Carvalho (2010) established two foundational theorems for the horseshoe prior: tight two-sided logarithmic bounds on the marginal density near the origin (Theorem~1.1), and a super-efficient rate of convergence of the Bayes predictive density to the true sampling density in sparse situations (Theorem~2). The ``Shrink Globally, Act Locally'' paper \citep{polson2010shrink} formalised necessary and sufficient conditions on the prior's behaviour at the origin for sparsity adaptation as $p \to \infty$. We show that these results are not merely descriptive properties of the horseshoe -- they are…
